response.text:
Dear Guest,
Thank you for your wonderful review and for choosing Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection.

We are truly honored to hear that, among the many 5-star hotels you have experienced in Ho Chi Minh City, your stay with us stands out as the best. Your recognition means a great deal to our entire team.

We are especially delighted that our service was the highlight of your visit. Delivering warm, personalized, and memorable hospitality is at the heart of everything we do, and it is rewarding to know that our associates made such a positive impression. We are also pleased that you enjoyed our modern facilities and well-appointed amenities, designed to provide both comfort and convenience throughout your stay.

Thank you once again for your kind words and recommendation. We are thrilled to know that we have earned your trust, and we look forward to welcoming you back to Vinpearl Landmark 81, Autograph Collection on your next trip to Ho Chi Minh City.

Warm regards,
Vinpearl L

value.description:
WhatsApp is a messaging app for personal and group communication through a direct, chat-based interface. It supports text messaging, voice calls, video calls, and media sharing, allowing real-time conversation between individuals or groups. Messages, attachments, and calls are handled within the same interface, without requiring separate tools. 

A chat list organizes ongoing conversations, showing recent activity and keeping frequently used threads accessible. Each chat supports text messages, images, videos, documents, voice notes, and location sharing. The interface presents these elements within a linear timeline that preserves context and makes exchanges easy to follow. Message indicators show when content has been sent, delivered, or viewed, giving users a clear sense of message status as interactions progress. 

Group functionality enables multi-party communication with tools for naming groups, assigning profile images, and managing participants. Administrators can add or remove members, adjust permissions, and determine who may send messages or modify group details. Groups support the same media types as individual chats, allowing coordinated sharing among teams, families, or other communities. Broadcast lists extend this system by sending one-to-many messages that appear as private conversations to recipients who have the sender’s number saved. 

Voice messages offer an alternative when typing is impractical. Users can record short or extended voice notes that appear directly in the chat timeline and can be played at adjustable speeds. The app also includes high-quality voice and video calling that operates through an internet connection. Calls support one-to-one conversations as well as group calls, giving users multiple ways to connect depending on context. 

Contact management draws on the device’s address book, allowing new chats to begin with minimal setup. A search function supports locating past messages, documents, links, and media by keyword, providing efficient retrieval of information from extended histories. Starred messages offer another retrieval method by marking important items for quick access. Together, these tools help maintain continuity in conversations that evolve over long periods. 

Media handling is central to the messaging experience. Photos, videos, and documents sent or received in chats can be viewed in galleries organized by file type, enabling users to revisit shared materials without scrolling through entire message histories. Forwarding options allow redistribution of items to other chats, with forwarding indicators helping recipients understand the origin of the content. Storage management tools assist in reviewing and removing large files or clearing specific chat histories to free device space. 

Privacy features offer granular control over visibility and interaction. Users can choose who may see their profile photo, status updates, and last-seen information. Read receipts can be enabled or disabled depending on communication preferences, and blocked contacts are prevented from calling or messaging. Two-step verification adds an optional security layer by requiring a PIN when registering the number on a new device. 

Status updates allow users to share photos, text, or short videos that remain visible for twenty-four hours to selected contacts. These updates appear in a separate section distinct from chats, keeping ephemeral content organized away from ongoing conversations. Viewership indicators show who has seen each update, while privacy controls define which contacts have access. 

Cross-device features support messaging on linked devices, allowing users to continue conversations from desktops or secondary devices once they authenticate through their phone. Linked devices maintain access even if the primary device temporarily loses connection, depending on service guidelines. This flexibility supports workflows in which typing on a larger screen or accessing shared files from a computer is preferable. 

Security is maintained through end-to-end encryption applied automatically to messages, calls, and media. This ensures that only the sender and recipient can access the contents of their communication. Encryption operates in the background and does not require manual configuration, providing a protected environment for everyday messaging without altering the interaction model familiar to users. 

Compatibility with Android devices allows the app to operate across a broad range of phones and tablets. It integrates with system-level notifications to surface incoming messages, calls, and media previews. Notification settings can be adjusted for individual chats or groups, offering flexibility for managing interruptions during work or personal time. 

Backup options support preserving chat histories, including messages, images, and other attachments. Users can enable automatic backups at chosen intervals or create them manually. Restoration from a backup allows chat data to reappear on a new device after number verification, dependent on backup availability and user settings. 

Additional tools refine the messaging experience. Wallpaper customization lets users set distinct backgrounds for specific chats or apply global themes. Data usage settings control media auto-download behavior, which can help manage bandwidth consumption in limited-data environments. These configurations allow users to tailor the app’s operation to their preferences while maintaining consistent communication capabilities. 

Group invitation controls and link management features offer structured options for admitting participants into group chats. Administrators can generate invitation links, reset them when necessary, or approve or deny join requests when restricted access is enabled. These controls help maintain group integrity and reduce unwanted additions. 

WhatsApp supports everyday communication through messaging, calling, and media sharing within a familiar chat-based environment. Its structure accommodates personal conversations, ongoing group discussions, and coordinated interaction, making it a consistent tool for routine communication across different contexts.

200.description:
One bid.cars lot from its server-rendered detail page `GET /en/lot/{lot}/{tag}`, addressed by lot id (`0-46008811`, `1-51374586`), by VIN (resolved through the site's `/app/search/en/vin-lot/{vin}/false` lookup) or by a pasted lot URL. Returns the Vehicle JSON-LD identity (year, make, model, VIN, colour, transmission, damages, sale date), the header (title, location, shipping terminal, seller, sale document, estimated value range), the bidding box (current bid and time left for active lots; `archived: true` with `auction_ended_on` and a hidden final bid for sold lots: the site masks final bids for anonymous users), the vehicle information block (loss, damages, odometer, start code, key, ACV/ERC, body, colour, engine, transmission, fuel, drive), the auction-house details list, the sales-history table and the image gallery. A lot the site does not know answers HTTP 410 and is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| --- | --- | --- |
| `archived` | boolean | The auction has ended and the page is the site's archived view. |
| `auction_ended_on` | string | Archived lots: the end date text, e.g. `Tuesday, June 16, 2026`. |
| `color` | string |  |
| `country` | string |  |
| `currency` | string |  |
| `current_bid_usd` | number | Active lots: the bidding box current bid (often $0 before the live auction). Null for archived lots. |
| `estimated_max_usd` | number |  |
| `estimated_min_usd` | number |  |
| `final_bid_hidden` | boolean | True when the site shows `Hidden` / masked instead of a final bid (anonymous view of a sold lot). |
| `final_bid_usd` | number | Archived lots: final bid when the site shows it; null while hidden. |
| `image` | string |  |
| `images` | string[] | Gallery thumbnails in the site's order. |
| `images_large` | string[] |  |
| `known_damages` | string |  |
| `live_auction_at` | string | Active lots: live auction date/time text, e.g. `Monday, 12 October, 15:30`. |
| `location` | string |  |
| `lot` | string |  |
| `make` | string |  |
| `model` | string |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `sale_date` | string | Sale date `YYYY-MM-DD` from the Vehicle JSON-LD (`purchaseDate`). |
| `sale_document` | string |  |
| `sales_history` | object[] | Rows of the Sales History table for this VIN; empty when the site has none. |
| `seller` | string |  |
| `seller_trusted` | boolean |  |
| `shipping_from` | string | Shipping terminal the site assigns. |
| `source` | string |  |
| `source_details` | object[] | The `Data fetched from the platform ...` list: label/value pairs as the auction house reports them (vary by house). |
| `source_lot_number` | string | The auction house's own lot / stock number. |

| `time_left` | string | Active lots: bidding-box countdown text at observation time. |
| `title` | string | Page lot title, e.g. `2018 BMW 3 Series, 330I`. |
| `transmission` | string |  |
| `url` | string |  |
| `vehicle` | object |  |
| `vin` | string |  |
| `year` | number |  |

provider.summary: Official provider example

post.description: Browse or filter lots currently at auction; find the lot id or VIN for `get_lot` and `similar_sold_lots`.

auction_type.description:
Source auction house (default All).

Provider reference: allowed values ["All", "Copart", "IAAI"].

body_style.description: Site body-style filter value (Sedan, SUV, Pickup, Hatchback, Coupe, Minivan, Crossover, Convertible, Cargo-Van, Van, Wagon).

continuation.description: Continuation from a previous call (`next_cursor`): the next page number. Overrides `page`. Pattern: ^[0-9]{1,4}$.

estimated_max.description:
Upper bound of the site's estimated value (USD).

Provider reference: minimum 0.

estimated_min.description:
Lower bound of the site's estimated value (USD).

Provider reference: minimum 0.

fuel_type.description: Site fuel-type filter value (Diesel, Electric, Hybrid).

limit.description:
Return at most this many lots from the page (the site always serves 50 per page; the rest of the page is dropped). Pagination is unaffected.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 50.

loss_type.description: Site loss-type filter value (Biohazard, Fire, Hail, Mechanical, Repossession, Theft, Vandalized, Water).

model.description: Model as listed by `makes_models` (e.g. `3 Series`); default `All`. Requires `make`.

order_by.description:
Site sort key (filter mode); omitted means the site's default order (sale date).

Provider reference: allowed values ["date", "dateDesc", "estimated", "estimatedDesc", "prebid", "prebidDesc", "buynow", "buynowDesc", "year", "yearDesc", "odometer", "odometerDesc"].

page.description:
1-based page of 50 lots (default 1).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 1000.

query.description: Free-text search (`search-type=typing`): make/model words, a VIN or a lot number. Mutually exclusive with the structured filters.

status.description:

blocks.text: A 42-year-old man killed while riding a roller-coaster at Six Flags Over Georgia was thrown from his seat and struck other patrons before landing below the ride, police said Tuesday.
Visitors to the Atlanta-area park watched in horror as he fell out of the coaster Monday, prompting Six Flags to temporarily close nine similar roller-coasters countrywide.
Investigators and park officials have not said how he ended up coming out of his seat.
"It was horrific to watch," said Summer Bates, who was at the park with her husband and three children. "One thing I think that will stick with us is the sound of his body coming down."

Bates said she and her family rode the Goliath roller-coaster earlier in the day. The park's tallest coaster, which towers over its entrance at 61 metres, has lap bar restraints that pull down over the riders' legs and waist. There are no seat belts.

"My older two children rode on the cart ahead of us," she said. "I noticed they kept trying to push theirs down tighter. I assured them that they were OK. But once my husband, youngest child and I loaded our cart and headed up the incline, I quickly understood why my older two were messing with theirs. It just didn't feel secure and tight."

The man who died was 42-year-old Hassan Jihad Ibn Kariem, according to Cobb County police. Officials have not released any other information about those who were injured when they were struck by the man.
Kariem worked as the information technology manager at a public charter school in Atlanta and before that was the school's technology teacher, according to an online resume.
Witness describes seeing man come out of his seat
Logan Conner said he was on the Goliath with his fiancée when he saw the man come out of his seat.
"The man started levitating in the air sideways," he told NBC. "We made direct eye contact with him."
WATCH | 1 dead, several injured in U.S. roller-coaster incident:
Britny Landry had been on the ride earlier Monday and was waiting in line to go again. She could see part of the Goliath track.
"We just look, and I just see somebody fly out," she told KTVU-TV. She said she wasn't sure if that's what she saw at first. "Maybe somebody had a bag or something."
Investigators say they spoke with park visitors and employees who saw what happened in the incident Monday at Six Flags Over Georgia in Mableton, about 24 kilometres northwest of Atlanta.
Coasters closed in Canada and U.S.

Nine roller-coasters at six North American parks that are similar to the coaster in Georgia were closed "out of an abundance of caution," according to a Six Flags Entertainment Corporation spokesperson, who said staff members and local authorities responded immediately and the park is co-operating with the investigation.
"We are deeply saddened by the guest incident at our park today," the spokesperson said, adding that the company is providing support to guests and staff who were impacted.

CBC News has confirmed that the list of nine rides includes the Behemoth and Leviathan at Canada's Wonderland, north of Toronto. A park spokesperson said it did not have a timeline for when the rides might be available again.
Canada's Wonderland is open to the public for 12 more Halloween-themed evenings and weekends until it closes for the winter.

Montreal's La Ronde amusement park said it was temporarily shutting down its Goliath roller-coaster until an update is received from the manufacturer of the ride. La Ronde was a Six Flags property until this spring, when the park's purchase by EPR Properties was finalized.
Authorities and Six Flags did not identify the roller-coaster at the Georgia location. However, local TV stations showed video of passengers being evacuated from the Goliath coaster.

The roller-coaster, which was opened in 2006, reaches top speeds of about 113 km/h and heights of 61 metres, the park's website reports. During about 3½ minutes, riders "navigate through razor-sharp turns and soar over colossal hills," according to the website.

"I cannot imagine the horror the patrons and employees witnessed today, and my heart aches for the family who lost a loved one," Lisa Cupid, chair of the Cobb County Board of Commissioners, said in a statement. She added that next of kin have been notified.
The amusement park is a major part of the county's tourism and brings in visitors from across the southeast, Cupid said.
"We are all grappling with how something so devastating could happen at a place that has given generations of families such happy memories," she said.

Georgia's Office of Insurance and Safety Fire Commissioner, which oversees ride inspections, is "conducting an in‑depth and comprehensive review," said Garrison Bennett, a spokesperson. The park was already scheduled to be closed Tuesday.

This death would be at least the seventh at the Georgia park, including one in 2006 in which a man had a likely heart attack on the Goliath coaster, according to the Doan Law Firm, which focuses on amusement park accidents.

It also comes less than two weeks after Six Flags Magic Mountain, in Southern California, announced that it is retiring its famous X2 roller-coaster amid lawsuits alleging serious brain injury caused by the ride. The park had settled one wrongful-death lawsuit from the family of a 22-year-old man who died after riding the coaster in 2022.

Last year, a 32-year-old man died after riding a high-speed roller-coaster at the Universal Epic Universe theme park in Florida. He died from blunt impact injuries, and his death was ruled accidental.

200.description:
Newest CBC items in one or more categories (sections or regions such as `edmonton`, `calgary`, `politics`, `world`) through CBC's aggregate_api `items` listing, optionally limited to a publish-date window (`from` / `to`, UTC calendar days, inclusive) and to content types (story, video). Sorted newest first by publish or last-update time; `page_size` up to 60. The API drops an unknown slug silently and would answer the whole site, so the function checks the API's `x-items-filters` echo: a slug CBC does not know is `not_found`, and every returned row is verified to carry a requested category. Rows are metadata only (title, deck, URL, publish and update instants, categories, media flags); use `get_article` for the text.

The response contains the tool result directly.

Returns the results grid as displayed: SCC entity_id, entity name, name type (Legal Name or Fictitious Name), entity type, series-LLC flag, principal office address, registered agent name, status, plus the site's internal numeric business_id that get_entity, get_entity_filings, get_entity_agent_history and get_entity_name_history take. 25 rows per page; the site's pager is session-bound, so page N re-runs the search and asks the pager for page N on the same session. A search with no match is a valid empty result (the site's 'No records found with your search criteria.'), not an error. One entity id can return many rows (one per legal and fictitious name).

The response contains the tool result directly.

The provider identifies `results` as the primary payload key.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `business_id` | string | The site's internal numeric id (from the row's SeriesLLC(id, ...) link), the key for get_entity, get_entity_filings, get_entity_agent_history and get_entity_name_history. |
| `entity_id` | string | Public SCC entity id as displayed (e.g. T0608648, F1725607, 11035161). |
| `entity_name` | string |  |
| `entity_type` | string | Entity type as displayed (Limited Liability Company, Stock Corporation, Nonstock Corporation, ...). |
| `name_type` | string | Legal Name, Fictitious Name, ... as displayed. |
| `principal_office_address` | string | One-line address as displayed; null when blank. |
| `registered_agent_name` | string | 'RA Name' column; null when blank. |
| `series_llc` | boolean | The 'Series LLC' column: true/false for limited liability companies, null when the site leaves it blank (other entity types). |
| `source_url` | string | The entity detail page for this row. |
| `status` | string | Status as displayed (Active, Inactive, Pending Active, Pending Inactive). |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Trade values, quantities and weights from the public preview of UN Comtrade (GET /public/v1/preview/{type}/{freq}/{classification}). One commodity code per call; the API accepts one period per request and silently caps each request at 500 records, so the function issues one request per requested period (up to 12, listed or as a range such as 2012-2019) and reports `truncated` per period. Partner omitted = breakdown by every partner; partner 0 = the reporter's world total. Values are USD as published (CIF for imports, FOB for exports); the full key-gated /data/v1 endpoint is not used.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | number | Total records across all periods. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number | Unix milliseconds when this result was fetched. |
| `periods` | object[] | One entry per requested period, in request order. |
| `records` | object[] |  |
| `request` | object | The selection as sent upstream (defaults filled in, periods expanded). |
| `truncated` | boolean | True when any period hit the 500-record preview cap; narrow the selection (partner, flow) or use fewer aggregates. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

Return public CMS procedure-volume rows by clinician NPI, including suppressed 1-10 counts as inclusive bounds, volume percentile where reported, and profile display indicator. | `count_min` | number | Inclusive lower bound: 1 for 1-10, exact volume for integers, null for ambiguous artifacts. |
| `count_reported` | string | Unmodified CMS count string. Scientific-notation source artifacts are kept here without an inferred exact count. |

| `volume_percentile` | number | Volume rank among clinicians performing the same category, not patient outcomes; null when CMS does not report it (including 1-10 counts). |

200.description:
Query rows of any DataSF dataset through the SODA 2.1 endpoint https://data.sf.gov/resource/<4x4>.json with SoQL: `select` (columns, aggregates such as count(*)), `where` (SoQL predicates incl. like, between, intersects(the_geom,'POINT(lon lat)'), within_circle(point, lat, lon, meters), within_box), `order`, `group`, `q` (full text) and `filters` (bare field=value equality parameters), paged with `limit` (1-50000, default 100) and `cursor` (row offset). Without `order` (and without `group`) the program orders by the row id `:id` so pages are stable. Rows come back exactly as published: numbers and dates are strings, geometry is GeoJSON; `columns` lists the returned field names and Socrata types from the X-SODA2-Fields/Types headers. An unknown dataset id is not_found; a SoQL error (unknown column, bad syntax) is invalid_input carrying the portal's message; an empty page is a successful result with count 0.

200.description:
Share of a geometry in each U.S. Drought Monitor category (None, D0 abnormally dry to D4 exceptional drought) on the current weekly map, with the counties it touches and their county-level shares. Exact when the geometry sits inside one category polygon (`spatial_precision: polygon`); when a category boundary crosses it, shares are estimated from up to 16 interior sample points (`grid_cell`). A Point gets the category at that point.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `categories` | object[] | Every category touching the geometry (plus `None` when part of it is in no category), worst first, with its share of the geometry in percent. Shares sum to 100. |
| `counties` | object[] | Counties intersecting the geometry (NDMC Counties layer) with their county-level categorical shares for the same map date from the USDM county statistics service. |
| `dominant` | string | Category with the largest share. |
| `in_drought` | boolean | True when any part of the geometry is in D1 or worse (D0 is abnormally dry, not drought). |
| `location` | object | Echo of the input geometry as parsed. |
| `map_date` | string | Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). |
| `method` | string | `within`: the whole polygon is inside one category polygon (exact). `intersects`: no category touches the polygon, so it is entirely `None` (exact). `point_sample`: a boundary crosses it; shares from interior sample points. `point`: a Point input. |
| `missing` | object[] | Layers that returned nothing for this geometry, with the reason, instead of guessed values. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `release_date` | string | Thursday the map was released; null when the geometry is in no category and the dates come from the county statistics row. |
| `sample_points` | number | Number of interior sample points behind `point_sample` shares; null otherwise. |
| `sources` | object[] |  |
| `spatial_precision` | string | How closely the values describe the geometry: `polygon` = exact against the source polygons; `grid_cell` = shares estimated from a grid of interior sample points; `county` = the value is for the county (or counties) containing the geometry; `point` = the value at a single point. |
| `valid_end` | string | Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). |
| `valid_start` | string | Calendar date, YYYY-MM-DD (UTC). |
| `worst` | string | Most severe category touching the geometry. |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Read one Senate eFD filing by report_kind and report_id (from search_reports), or by its pasted efdsearch.senate.gov/search/view/ URL. Four detail families: ptr (GET /search/view/ptr/{id}/): title, filer name, filed-at text and date, the certification statements, and the transactions table (number, date, owner, ticker or null, asset name, asset type, transaction type, amount range text with parsed min/max dollars, comment or null); annual (GET /search/view/annual/{id}/, also Candidate reports and amendments): title, filer, filed-at, certifications and every Part section (number, title, yes/no question and answer, the table's column headers and rows as text cells, notes); paper (GET /search/view/paper/{id}/, scanned filings incl. all blind-trust and other-document reports): page_count and pages[] with the page image URL on efd-media-public.senate.gov (anonymous GIFs, not fetched); extension_notice (GET /search/view/extension-notice/regular/{id}/): filer name, notice text and the new due date. Filed-at timestamps carry no timezone on the page and are kept as text plus the calendar date. Sections not applicable to the family are omitted. An unknown report_id is answered by the site with a redirect to the search form and reported as not_found. LEGAL NOTICE (5 U.S.C. app. 105(c)): it is unlawful to obtain or use a report for any unlawful purpose; for any commercial purpose other than by news and communications media for dissemination to the general public; for determining or establishing the credit rating of any individual; or for use, directly or indirectly, in the solicitation of money for any political, charitable or other purpose. The caller must set acknowledge_use_prohibitions to true; otherwise the function fails with invalid_input and contacts nothing.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `certifications` | object[] | ptr, annual: the statements the filer checked (or left unchecked) before filing. |
| `extension` | object | extension_notice only. |
| `filed_at_text` | string | ptr, annual: the 'Filed MM/DD/YYYY @ h:mm AM/PM' stamp as rendered; no timezone is stated on the page. |
| `filed_date` | string | ptr, annual: calendar date of filed_at_text. |
| `filer_name` | string | ptr, annual, extension_notice: the filer as named on the page (e.g. 'The Honorable Sheldon Whitehouse (Whitehouse, Sheldon)'). Omitted for paper filings, whose pages carry no name. |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `page_count` | number | paper only. |
| `pages` | object[] | paper only: scanned page images in order. |
| `parts` | object[] | annual only: every section of the report in page order (Part 1 .. Part 10, then Attachments & Comments). |
| `prohibitions_notice` | string |  |

post.description: Find Senate financial disclosure filings (PTRs, annual reports, extensions, blind trusts, paper filings) by Senator or candidate name, state, report type or date, and obtain report_id values for get_report.

acknowledge_use_prohibitions.description: Must be true: the caller affirms the prohibitions on obtaining and using financial disclosure reports in 5 U.S.C. app. 105(c) (no unlawful or commercial use other than by news media, no credit rating, no solicitation of money). The program submits the site's acknowledgement only on the caller's behalf after this affirmation.

candidate_state.description: Two-letter state code of the candidate's race. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

continuation.description: Opaque cursor from a previous page's meta.page.next_cursor (the next start offset). Pattern: ^\d{1,7}$.

filer_types.description: Restrict to filer types (site codes 1, 4, 5). Empty or absent: all.

filter_text.description: Free-text filter applied by the site across all result columns (the DataTables search box); records_filtered reflects it.

last_name.description: Filer last name, prefix match as on the site (for example 'Warren').

page_size.description:
Rows per page, 1-100 (the site's maximum).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 100; default 25.

report_types.description: Restrict to report types: annual (Annual and Candidate reports incl. amendments, code 7), ptr (Periodic Transaction Reports, 11), extension (Due Date Extension notices, 10), blind_trust (14), other (Other Documents, 15). Empty or absent: all.

senator_state.description: Two-letter state code of the Senator's seat. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

sort_by.description:
Sort column. Default date_received.

Provider reference: allowed values ["first_name", "last_name", "filer", "report", "date_received"]; default "date_received".

sort_dir.description:
Sort direction. Default desc (newest first).

Provider reference: allowed values ["asc", "desc"]; default "desc".

submitted_from.description: Earliest date received, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive). Default 2012-01-01, the site's minimum. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

submitted_to.description: Latest date received, YYYY-MM-DD (inclusive, through 23:59:59). Default: open-ended. Pattern: ^\d{4}-\d{2}-\d{2}$.

on the right of citizens of the Union and their family members to move and reside freely within the territory of the Member States amending Regulation (EEC) No 1612/68 and repealing Directives 64/221/EEC, 68/360/EEC, 72/194/EEC, 73/148/EEC, 75/34/EEC, 75/35/EEC, 90/364/EEC, 90/365/EEC and 93/96/EEC

(Text with EEA relevance)

THE EUROPEAN PARLIAMENT AND THE COUNCIL OF THE EUROPEAN UNION,

Having regard to the Treaty establishing the European Community, and in particular Articles 12, 18, 40, 44 and 52 thereof,

Having regard to the proposal from the Commission (1),

Having regard to the Opinion of the European Economic and Social Committee (2),

Having regard to the Opinion of the Committee of the Regions (3),

Acting in accordance with the procedure laid down in Article 251 of the Treaty (4),

Whereas:

(1)

Citizenship of the Union confers on every citizen of the Union a primary and individual right to move and reside freely within the territory of the Member States, subject to the limitations and conditions laid down in the Treaty and to the measures adopted to give it effect.

(2)

The free movement of persons constitutes one of the fundamental freedoms of the internal market, which comprises an area without internal frontiers, in which freedom is ensured in accordance with the provisions of the Treaty.

(3)

Union citizenship should be the fundamental status of nationals of the Member States when they exercise their right of free movement and residence. It is therefore necessary to codify and review the existing Community instruments dealing separately with workers, self-employed persons, as well as students and other inactive persons in order to simplify and strengthen the right of free movement and residence of all Union citizens.

(4)

With a view to remedying this sector-by-sector, piecemeal approach to the right of free movement and residence and facilitating the exercise of this right, there needs to be a single legislative act to amend Council Regulation (EEC) No 1612/68 of 15 October 1968 on freedom of movement for workers within the Community (5) and to repeal the following acts: Council Directive 68/360/EEC of 15 October 1968 on the abolition of restrictions on movement and residence within the Community for workers of Member States and their families (6), Council Directive 73/148/EEC of 21 May 1973 on the abolition of restrictions on movement and residence within the Community for nationals of Member States with regard to establishment and the provision of services (7), Council Directive 90/364/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the right of residence (8), Council Directive 90/365/EEC of 28 June 1990 on the right of residence for employees and self-employed persons who have ceased their occupational activity (9) and Council Directive 93/96/EEC of 29 October 1993 on the right of residence for students (10).

(5)

The right of all Union citizens to move and reside freely within the territory of the Member States should, if it is to be exercised under objective conditions of freedom and dignity, be also granted to their family members, irrespective of nationality. For the purposes of this Directive, the definition of "family member" should also include the registered partner if the legislation of the host Member State treats registered partnership as equivalent to marriage.

(6)

In order to maintain the unity of the family in a broader sense and without prejudice to the prohibition of discrimination on grounds of nationality, the situation of those persons who are not included in the definition of family members under this Directive, and who therefore do not enjoy an automatic right of entry and residence in the host Member State, should be examined by the host Member State on the basis of its own national legislation, in order to decide whether entry and residence could be granted to such persons, taking into consideration their relationship with the Union citizen or any other circumstances, such as their financial or physical dependence on the Union citizen.

(7)

The formalities connected with the free movement of Union citizens within the territory of Member States should be clearly defined, without prejudice to the provisions applicable to national border controls.

(8)

With a view to facilitating the free movement of family members who are not nationals of a Member State, those who have already obtained a residence card should be exempted from the requirement to obtain an entry visa within the meaning of Council Regulation (EC) No 539/2001 of 15 March 2001 listing the third countries whose nationals must be in possession of visas when crossing the external borders and those whose nationals are exempt from that requirement (11) or, where appropriate, of the applicable national legislation.

(9)

Union citizens should have the right of residence in the host Member State for a period not exceeding three months without being subject to any conditions or any formalities other than the requirement to hold a valid identity card or passport, without prejudice to a more favourable treatment applicable to job-seekers as recognised by the case-law of the Court of Justice.

(10)

Persons exercising their right of residence should not, however, become an unreasonable burden on the social assistance system of the host Member State during an initial period of residence. Therefore, the right of residence for Union citizens and their family members for periods in excess of three months should be subject to conditions.

(11)

The fundamental and personal right of residence in another Member State is conferred directly on Union citizens by the Treaty and is not dependent upon their having fulfilled administrative procedures.

(12)

For periods of residence of longer than three months, Member States should have the possibility to require Union citizens to register with the competent authorities in the place of residence, attested by a registration certificate issued to that effect.

(13)

The residence card requirement should be restricted to family members of Union citizens who are not nationals of a Member State for periods of residence of longer than three months.

(14)

The supporting documents required by the competent authorities for the issuing of a registration certificate or of a residence card should be comprehensively specified in order to avoid divergent administrative practices or interpretations constituting an undue obstacle to the exercise of the right of residence by Union citizens and their family members.

(15)

Family members should be legally safeguarded in the event of the death of the Union citizen, divorce, annulment of marriage or termination of a registered partnership. With due regard for family life and human dignity, and in certain conditions to guard against abuse, measures should therefore be taken to ensure that in such circumstances family members already residing within the territory of the host Member State retain their right of residence exclusively on a personal basis.

(16)

As long as the beneficiaries of the right of residence do not become an unreasonable burden on the social assistance system of the host Member State they should not be expelled. Therefore, an expulsion measure should not be the automatic consequence of recourse to the social assistance system. The host Member State should examine whether it is a case of temporary difficulties and take into account the duration of residence, the personal circumstances and the amount of aid granted in order to consider whether the beneficiary has become an unreasonable burden on its social assistance system and to proceed to his expulsion. In no case should an expulsion measure be adopted against workers, self-employed persons or job-seekers as defined by the Court of Justice save on grounds of public policy or public security.

(17)

Enjoyment of permanent residence by Union citizens who have chosen to settle long term in the host Member State would strengthen the feeling of Union citizenship and is a key element in promoting social cohesion, which is one of the fundamental objectives of the Union. A right of permanent residence should therefore be laid down for all Union citizens and their family members who have resided in the host Member State in compliance with the conditions laid down in this Directive during a continuous period of five years without becoming subject to an expulsion measure.

(18)

In order to be a genuine vehicle for integration into the society of the host Member State in which the Union citizen resides, the right of permanent residence, once obtained, should not be subject to any conditions.

(19)

Certain advantages specific to Union citizens who are workers or self-employed persons and to their family members, which may allow these persons to acquire a right of permanent residence before they have resided five years in the host Member State, should be maintained, as these constitute acquired rights, conferred by Commission Regulation (EEC) No 1251/70 of 29 June 1970 on the right of workers to remain in the territory of a Member State after having been employed in that State (12) and Council Directive 75/34/EEC of 17 December 1974 concerning the right of nationals of a Member State to remain in the territory of another Member State after having pursued therein an activity in a self-employed capacity (13).

records.description: SBH | Schulbau Hamburg hat als Landesbetrieb der Freien und Hansestadt Hamburg (nachstehend SBH genannt) die Aufgabe, die Schulimmobilien unter Berücksichtigung der schulischen Belange nach wirtschaftlichen Grundsätzen zu planen, zu bauen, zu unterhalten und zu bewirtschaften und die mehr als 400 Schulen an die Behörde für Schule und Berufsbildung (BSB) zu vermieten. --------------- Am Standort Hebebrandstr. 1 ist die Neugründung einer 6-zügigen Campusschule geplant. Die Neugründung des Schulstandortes erfordert die Errichtung einer Dreifeldsporthalle. Diese soll auf dem zukünftig entstehenden Baufeld des abzureißenden Gebäudes 05 entstehen. Die Sporthalle wird als Versammlungsstätte geplant und muss den Anforderungen des Denkmalschutzes entsprechen. --------------- Hier: Maler --------------- Bei der Sporthalle handelt es sich um eine Dreifeld-Halle mit Schul- und Vereinsnutzung, inkl. Nebenräume. Der Sporthallenbau ist zweigeschossig ausgebildet und erhält eine Tribüne die über zwei Treppen zu erreichen ist. Neben der Haupterschließung der Halle über Eingänge von außen ist der Neubau mittels eines geschlossenen Brückenbauwerks vom Bestandsbau aus zugänglich. Die Sporthalle ist als Versammlungsstätte deklariert. Die Sporthalle ist als Stahlbeton-Massivbau konzipiert und wird flach gegründet. Es sind Malerarbeiten gem. LV zu errichten.

200.description:
The complete FoodData Central record of one food by FDC id (GET /portal-data/external/{fdcId}, the web portal's own backend; also accepts a pasted fdc.nal.usda.gov/food-details/{fdcId}/... URL). Returns identity (data type, NDB number / FNDDS food code / GTIN-UPC, category, publication and update dates), every nutrient with its per-100 g value, unit, data points, min/max/median, derivation and source, portions with gram weights, nutrient conversion factors, ontology attributes (FoodOn, NCBI taxon), the Survey input foods, and for Branded foods the brand, ingredients, serving size and label nutrients. Section-header rows without a value (e.g. 'Proximates') and the per-sample laboratory analysis details of Foundation foods are not returned; `analyses` counts them. Missing optional fields are null. An unknown id is `not_found`.

The response contains the tool result directly.

| Documented field | Provider type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `attributes` | object[] | Distinct (name, value) food attributes: FoodOn / NCBI taxon ontology links, WWEIA category, Branded change notes. |
| `brand` | object | Branded foods only; null for other data types. |
| `conversion_factors` | object[] |  |
| `data_type` | string | Foundation, SR Legacy, Survey (FNDDS), Branded or Experimental, as the portal's foodType. |
| `description` | string |  |
| `fdc_id` | number |  |
| `food_category` | object | Foundation / SR Legacy food group, Survey WWEIA category, or the Branded GPC category group (description only). |
| `food_class` | string | The portal's foodClass (FinalFood, Survey, Branded). |
| `food_code` | string | Survey (FNDDS) food code; null for other data types (the portal's literal 'null' string is mapped to null). |
| `gtin_upc` | string |  |
| `is_historical_reference` | boolean |  |
| `label_nutrients` | object | Branded foods only: the Nutrition Facts label values per serving keyed by the portal's label names (calories, fat, saturatedFat, transFat, cholesterol, sodium, carbohydrates, fiber, sugars, protein, calcium, iron, ...); passed through as the portal names them. Null for other data types. |
| `last_updated` | string | M/D/YYYY as the portal formats it. |
| `ndb_number` | string |  |
| `nutrient_count` | number |  |
| `nutrients` | object[] |  |
| `observed_at_ms` | number |  |
| `portions` | object[] |  |
| `published_date` | string | Publication date as the portal formats it (M/D/YYYY); null where the record carries none (Foundation, SR Legacy). |
| `source_url` | string |  |
| `survey` | object | Survey (FNDDS) foods only: the WWEIA cycle dates and the SR foods the recipe is built from. |
| `total_refuse` | number |  |
| `url` | string |  |


These are the provider's documented fields. Field requiredness, nullability and nested object structures are specified only where the descriptions explicitly say so.

200.description:
Search FoodData Central foods (POST /portal-data/external/search, the web portal's own backend) by free text across one or more data types (Foundation, SR Legacy, Survey (FNDDS), Branded, Experimental). The text matches descriptions, brand owners, ingredients and GTIN/UPC codes; an empty query lists every food of the selected data types (e.g. all ~400 Foundation foods), sorted by description or published date. 50 results per page; `total_hits` and `counts_by_data_type` report how many foods match in every data type regardless of the filter. Each result carries the FDC id that `get_food` takes, the data-type specific identifier (NDB number, FNDDS food code or GTIN/UPC), brand and category fields where the data type has them (null otherwise) and, when `include_nutrients` is true, the per-100 g nutrient values the portal returns with every result. A page past the last page is `not_found`; a query with no match is a valid empty result.

availability_date.description: Venue-local date, YYYY-MM-DD. Adds each matching service's available start times for that day and keeps only venues with availability. Pattern: ^[0-9]{4}-[0-9]{2}-[0-9]{2}$.

availability_start_time_from.description: Earliest start time HH:MM (24h, venue-local). Needs availability_date. Pattern: ^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$.

availability_start_time_to.description: Latest start time HH:MM (24h, venue-local). Needs availability_date. Pattern: ^[0-9]{2}:[0-9]{2}$.

treatment_id.description: Taxonomy id from autocomplete.taxonomy[].id: `tag:eyelash-extensions`, `category:massage` or a treatment type `treatment:eyebrows-and-eyelashes/hybrid-lash-extensions`. Pattern: ^((tag|category|type):[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*|treatment:[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*/[a-z0-9]+(-[a-z0-9]+)*)$.

Gas system in transition: security of supply - interim response

value.body_markdown:
This consultation is inviting views and supporting evidence on our assessment of the priorities for gas security of supply during the transition, and the associated challenges facing the gas sector. It sets out a range of proposed policy actions that we are considering in order to protect our gas security in the years ahead.

We committed to a programme of public engagement on the gas system’s transition in the [June 2025 update to market](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/midstream-gas-system-update-to-the-market/midstream-gas-system-update-to-the-market). This consultation is the first step in this programme of work.

This represents a significant milestone in our commitment to shape a gas system that provides energy security for decades to come. It covers:

- our understanding of the changing patterns of gas supply and demand and how we expect these to evolve during the energy transition, including the continuing need for peak-day capacity
- our three-point plan for gas security of supply, which includes:
  1. accelerating decarbonisation to secure energy for the long term
  2. taking the necessary steps to ensure the gas system and market can adapt to continue providing baseload gas supply and insurance for low probability, high stress events
  3. continuing to work with National Gas and NESO to monitor our security of supply and utilising the range of tools available to continue to match supply and demand, to balance the system on a daily basis now and for years to come
- our three priorities to ensure the gas system and market can adapt to provide supply in a range of scenarios:
  1. maintaining sufficient infrastructure capacity
  2. maintaining sufficient infrastructure resilience
  3. a commercial model that supports effective infrastructure operation
- the current picture of our midstream gas infrastructure (LNG, interconnectors, storage) and a range of government policy actions that could be taken to ensure we have sufficient infrastructure to provide gas whenever and wherever it is needed
- further government policy actions designed to ensure a commercial model that works, both in terms of ensuring the commercial viability of existing infrastructure operators and exploring how regulatory and market-based changes could support the UK’s continued attractiveness to land gas imports

The territorial extent of this consultation is Great Britain only given energy policy is devolved to Northern Ireland and they have an independently operated gas system. However, given Northern Ireland’s reliance on gas supplies from Great Britain, we are committed to working closely with them on the issues outlined in this consultation.

Read our [consultation privacy notice](https://www.gov.uk/government/publications/desnz-consultations-privacy-notice/privacy-notice-relating-to-consultation-responses-received-by-desnz).

value.name: Nolla A-Frames Near Yosemite
value.overview:
Off-Grid A-Frame Glamping Near Yosemite 🌄🛖

Tucked just 15 miles east of Groveland and about 20 minutes from the Yosemite National Park entrance, our modern A-frame cabins offer a unique, off-grid experience for those who want a little more comfort than a tent — without giving up the adventure.

Designed by the Finnish group Nolla, these minimalist and cozy cabins are built to help you unplug and unwind. Each cabin is well insulated, includes fresh linens, and Rumpl blankets to keep you warm.

Perfect for couples, small families, or close-knit friends, the cabin can be arranged as either two twin beds or a king-sized bed to accommodate up to four people. Whether you’re here for a romantic getaway under the stars or a no-frills glamping basecamp for Yosemite exploration, these cabins offer a mix of simplicity and comfort.

Each A-frame is equipped with solar power for small device charging, a portable fan, and access to an odorless composting toilet (cabin 2,3) or a pottery (cabin 1) near the cabin. The cabins also have access to hot showers and flushing toilets across the highway at our sister property. It’s a true step off the beaten path and into a more immersive experience.

The cabins include a bed, shelter from the elements, and solar-powered lighting and charging. Because this is a rustic glamping experience, the cabin doors do not lock. We are located in a quiet, remote setting, and guests should plan accordingly. 

 • Cabin 1: Easily accessible for most vehicles. 

 • Cabins 2 and 3: A bit more adventurous — AWD or 4x4 recommended during rain or wet conditions.

Note that when temperatures in Groveland are above 90 degrees, the cabins do get quite warm. The best ways we have found to manage the heat is by leaving the doors open during the day (with the screen door closed), curtain closed, and fan on all day. 

If you're looking for a cozy basecamp that combines the comfort of a cabin with the spirit of camping, you'll feel right at home here.

review_summaries.summary: This campsite offers a cozy and convenient base for exploring Yosemite National Park. Guests frequently mention the stunning views, from sunrises to starry nights, enhancing the tranquil atmosphere. The cabins are praised for their cleanliness and comfort, though some visitors noted minor issues like cobwebs or ants. Access to clean showers and proximity to the park entrance are appreciated, making it a practical choice for nature lovers.

The campsite offers a clean and well-maintained bathroom experience, which many guests appreciated after a long day exploring Yosemite. While most found the facilities to be spotless, a few guests noted the presence of cobwebs, which could be improved. The showers, available at a nearby sister property, were highlighted as a convenient perk, providing a refreshing end to the day. Overall, the bathroom facilities were a hit for those seeking comfort in nature.

The campsite warmly welcomes pets, making it a perfect getaway for travelers who want to bring their furry companions along. Reviews indicate that pet owners had a delightful experience, with plenty of space for dogs to roam. While some pets might get a bit dusty from the red clay, the overall stay remains enjoyable. The hosts ensure that pet-friendly accommodations are comfortable for both pets and their humans.

The campsite provides a sense of seclusion and privacy, ideal for those looking to escape the hustle and bustle. Many guests appreciated the quiet and peaceful environment, which allowed for a relaxing retreat. While some cabins are near each other, they are positioned to maintain privacy, creating a serene atmosphere. Overall, the campsite offers a tranquil getaway surrounded by nature's beauty.

The hosts, Liza and Tom, are consistently praised for their hospitality and attentiveness. Guests found them to be responsive and accommodating, enhancing the overall experience. Their efforts to provide clear directions and helpful tips were particularly appreciated. The personalized service from the hosts contributes to a welcoming and enjoyable stay.

Nestled close to Yosemite, the campsite offers easy access to the park's wonders. Guests highlighted the proximity to Yosemite's entrance, making it an excellent base for day trips. The surroundings provide stunning views that enhance the camping experience. With nearby amenities and nature spots, the location is both practical and picturesque.

Families found the campsite to be a delightful retreat, catering well to both adults and kids. The cabins provide a cozy and comfortable environment, making it ideal for family bonding. The serene surroundings and engaging nature experiences create lasting memories for all ages. The site is well-suited for family outings, offering both adventure and relaxation.

sites.name: Cabin 1
sites.overview: Cabin 1 is our most accessible site, while still offering plenty of privacy and quiet. It is a short drive to this site, and offers beautiful views, a picnic table, and a composting toilet. This Nolla Cabin has 2 Twin beds, or you can convert them into a King sized bed by adding our provided planks in between. Perfect for a couple, two friends, or a family of 4 (with young kids). The cabin includes a solar battery (enough to charge your devices and more). We will provide bedding: sheets, pillows, and cozy Rumpl blankets.

sites.name: Cabin 2
sites.overview: Cabin 2 is located near Cabin 3. While still offering privacy from one another, separated by trees, these Nolla Cabins are also a good option if traveling with a group. Cabin 2 is farther back on the property, tucked away near a stream. You will truly feel like you are in the wilderness here. There is a picnic table and Yeti cooler provided, as well as a composting toilet, shared by Cabin 3. During the rainy season, All Wheel or 4 Wheel Drive is required to access this cabin. The cabin includes a solar battery (enough to charge your devices and more). We will provide bedding: sheets, pillows, and cozy Rumple blankets.

reviews.text: Lovely spot in a quiet neighborhood within a hourish drive to Yosemite
The site was lovely, and the hosts were very kind. I would recommend this to anyone. Very great location too, about an hour out from the park.
Wonderful hosts! Great little camping place and very affordable!

I’m always hesitant to rave about someplace I’ve stayed for fear more campers will come and it will no longer be available to book in the future.  However, Meadow View Haven was an absolutely beautiful location with all the amenities needed for me to stay while visiting family in the area.  The host(s) were very responsive to any questions I had.  I would highly recommend staying here.  Just one note: bring extra sewer lines as the sewer port was far away after finding the most level spot.
reviews.title: Beautiful location

reviews.text: Directions were clear. Good place to Camp of you are planning to visit Yosemite
reviews.title: Flexible check in time

reviews.text: Easy place to car camp before heading to Yosemite. Didn’t meet the host because we arrived late and left early but was easy to find and set up for the night. Would stay again
We had a very pleasant stay. The hosts were kind, helpful, and easy to communicate with. Everything went smoothly, and we appreciated having a great and peaceful spot for our RV. Thank you.
reviews.title: Pleasant stay with helpful hosts

reviews.text: Our hosts were wonderful and the site was perfect. Thank you so much!

I loved camping on Kiya’s land! I know a lot of people talked about using this spot as a prep/debrief launch pad before or after their trip to Yosemite, but I used it as my base camp. 

It was so nice to have a quiet space all to myself away from the insane crowds and packed campgrounds in the park. 

The drive in was an hour to the entrances, but that gave me time to reflect on my trip, get psyched with a playlist, and have my breakfast! Seeing the sun set on the way out of the park was so beautiful every day, and it was so peaceful. For context, I wanna mention that I love driving. 

About their site: I definitely overpacked, because they have water access and a power outlet to charge your devices/lights etc. There is also an outdoor makeshift bathroom for you to use which was a really considerate touch! The solar panels nearby are perfect to put things you want to keep dry under, but be mindful of the separations between panels, as rain may sprinkle down in between them. 

I felt very welcome there, they came out to check on me the first night I was there, and even gave me some recommendations on where to go in the park, and even was left a friendly note giving me a head’s up about some rain on the way so my gear wouldn’t get soaked! Very gracious, warm, and considerate. 

I would absolutely come back again, I want more time to check out not only the park but also what Mariposa has to offer. 

A perfect spot for both a couple days or spending the night when passing through
reviews.title: Yosemite Adjacent Oasis

reviews.text: Extremely sweet and accommodating hosts. Easy directions/instructions for staying at their site which is in such a quiet, gorgeous area. The animals on property were also amazing. Would definitely recommend staying here and hope to stay again in the future if we're ever in the area.
reviews.title: Perfect,little spot with great host

reviews.text: The hosts were fantastic and had wonderful hospitality. They responded quickly every time I had a question.

My second time staying here in a week. It's a great spot to get things done before going into Yosemite and out of Yosemite which I did both times. I couldn't go in at the closest entrance from this hip camp because the HWY was closed due to a rock slide, but going through the South entrance instead was fine. The host is super responsive and nice.

This is a great spot with FULL hookup in Mariposa. I love staying at places with all the amenities so I can do a full reset of the van before I head into a national park. Host was super helpful and accommodating. I'm staying again when I leave Yosemite.
reviews.title: Great spot near Yosemite

post.description: Search kbb.com dealer and private-seller inventory for a make (optionally model and trim) within a radius of a US ZIP code, optionally filtered by year, price, maximum mileage, exterior colour and drivetrain. Returns one page of 25 listings with price, KBB Fair Purchase Price and deal rating, mileage, VIN, seller and distance, plus the total match count for pagination.

drive_type.description:
Drivetrain group. kbb.com groups AWD and 4WD together, so awd and 4wd return the same listings (drive_type AWD4WD).

Provider reference: allowed values ["awd", "4wd", "fwd", "rwd"].

exterior_color.description:
kbb.com exterior colour group; matches the manufacturer colour names in `exterior_color` (e.g. white matches Snowflake White Pearl Mica).

Provider reference: allowed values ["beige", "black", "blue", "brown", "burgundy", "charcoal", "gold", "gray", "green", "off_white", "orange", "pink", "purple", "red", "silver", "tan", "turquoise", "white", "yellow"].

listing_type.description:
Inventory to search: used, new, certified pre-owned, or all three. Defaults to used.

Provider reference: allowed values ["used", "new", "certified", "all"]; default "used".

make.description: kbb.com make slug, e.g. toyota, honda, ford, mercedes-benz.

mileage_max.description:
Only listings with at most this many miles on the odometer (kbb.com maxMileage filter; any ceiling, not just the site's 10,000-mile steps).

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 999999.

model.description: kbb.com model slug, e.g. camry, civic, f150, model-3. Powertrain variants are not separate models (Kona Electric is kona, Bolt EV is bolt); an unknown slug fails with not_found naming the make's valid slugs. Omit for all models of the make.

page.description:
Result page; 25 listings per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 40; default 1.

price_max.description:
Highest advertised price to include, in whole US dollars; must not be below price_min.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

price_min.description:
Lowest advertised price to include, in whole US dollars.

Provider reference: minimum 0.

radius_miles.description:
Search radius in miles; 0 means nationwide. KBB pads a market's results with remote 'virtual dealer' delivery listings whose distance is not the seller's; with a non-zero radius these are excluded (count may be below page_size while total_count still includes them).

Provider reference: allowed values ["0", "10", "25", "50", "75", "100", "200", "300", "400", "500"]; default 50.

sort.description:
Result order: relevance (KBB default), price_asc / price_desc by KBB derived price (advertised price plus fees, so advertised prices are only approximately ordered), mileage_asc, year_desc (newest model year first), distance_asc (nearest seller first), newest (most recently listed first).

Provider reference: allowed values ["relevance", "price_asc", "price_desc", "mileage_asc", "year_desc", "distance_asc", "newest"]; default "relevance".

trim.description: Trim name as shown in listings (e.g. SE, XLE, Sport Touring). Requires model.

year_max.description:
Newest model year to include, inclusive; must not be below year_min.

Provider reference: minimum 1981; maximum 2030.

year_min.description:
Oldest model year to include, inclusive.

Provider reference: minimum 1981; maximum 2030.

zip.description: Five-digit US ZIP code at the centre of the search. Pattern: ^[0-9]{5}$.

post.description: Pass a Letterboxd film URL or boxd.it link (`url`), a slug (`slug`), a boxd.it id (`lid`), a TMDB id (`tmdb_id`) or an IMDb id (`imdb_id`); exactly one. For many films at once use ratings_bulk; for the histogram and watched/list/like counts use film_ratings; for member reviews use reviews (sort `popular` is the film page's Popular reviews strip); for lists use lists.

imdb_id.description: IMDb title id; resolved through letterboxd.com/imdb/<id>/. Pattern: ^tt[0-9]+$.

lid.description: Letterboxd short id, the path of a boxd.it link (case-sensitive). Pattern: ^[A-Za-z0-9]+$.

slug.description: Film slug from the URL path, e.g. parasite-2019 (the year suffix is part of the slug when Letterboxd uses one). A bare title slug such as parasite or sentimental-value belongs to whichever film took that slug first, often an older film with the same title; when the slug is not known from a Letterboxd URL, pass tmdb_id or imdb_id, or take the slug from search_films, and confirm name and year in the output. Pattern: ^[a-z0-9-]+$.

tmdb_id.description: TMDB movie id; resolved through letterboxd.com/tmdb/<id>/. Pattern: ^[0-9]+$.

url.description: Letterboxd film page URL (https://letterboxd.com/film/<slug>/...) or boxd.it short link (https://boxd.it/<lid>). Pattern: ^https?://(www\.)?(letterboxd\.com/film/[a-z0-9-]+|boxd\.it/[A-Za-z0-9]+).

IMDB's top 250 list: loved by some, hated by others. Of course you can argue about the order of movies and the presence or absence of certain titles. Fact remains that it holds a great deal of the most appreciated films of all time and the overall quality is pretty high.

I tried to complete the list once, but choked near the end... ;-) I will keep updating weekly though and one day I will finish the last few missing films.

Feel free to comment your % or must sees from this list!
And for the people who find 250 entries a bit lacking, here's a list with every movie that was once in IMDB's Top 250.

A few statistics...

The oldest movie on the list is Charlie Chaplin's The Kid, released in 1921. The most popular decade in the list is the 2000's with 49 entries. A complete overview:
1920's - 6 entries
1930's - 6 entries
1940's - 9 entries
1950's - 21 entries
1960's - 16 entries
1970's - 19 entries
1980's - 25 entries
1990's - 39 entries
2000's - 49 entries
2010's - 41 entries
2020's - 19 entries

Christopher Nolan is the king of IMDB, with 9 films on the top 250. There are three directors with 7 films on the list. Scorsese, Kubrick and Spielberg complete the crème de la crème according to IMDB users.

All popular directors:
9 entries - Christopher Nolan
7 entries - Stanley Kubrick, Steven Spielberg, Martin Scorsese
6 entries - Akira Kurosawa, Quentin Tarantino
5 entries - Billy Wilder, Charlie Chaplin, Alfred Hitchcock
4 entries - Hayao Miyazaki, Sergio Leone
3 entries - Brad Bird, Clint Eastwood, David Fincher, Francis Ford Coppola, James Cameron, Joel Coen, Pete Docter, Peter Jackson, Ridley Scott, Denis Villeneuve


Latest update: 28/9/2026. I am currently at 98%

Gone, not forgotten:
Andhadhun

Update: Now in video form

There is a house on a hill, and there are people in it. And they're nice, but not really. There is a garden, and there they get a lot of sunlight. And it is nice, and they get to sleep there sometimes.

There is a house underground, and there are people in it. And they're the first to tell you that they're not very nice: they're con-men, grifters, forgers and imposters. They sit among stink bugs, and they've been there for so long that maybe they've convinced themselves that they just belong there.

There is a rock, and it is a gift, but it is also a burden. And maybe it's a metaphor, but it's also just a rock: solid and heavy, difficult to lug around, and dangerous in the wrong hands. Some people will tell you that it's supposed to bring wealth. But again, it's also just a rock.

There is a line, and it cannot be crossed.

There is a smell, and it comes from the underground. And the people who live in the house on the hill can smell it. And the people who live underground try to imagine a life in the sun, a future where they aren't just garbage to be washed away in the rain. But there is a smell that sticks to them, and they know that they can never really belong.

There is a world, and it is nice, but not really. There are houses on hills, and houses underground. There is plenty of sun, but it isn't for everybody. There are people grateful to be slaves, and people unhappy to be served. There are systems that we are born into, and they create these lines that cannot be crossed. And we all dream of something better, but we've been living with these lines for so long that we've convinced ourselves that there really isn't anything to be done.

There is a knife. And it doesn't do much in the long run, but there will always be some satisfaction in crossing some lines.

A search with no match is a valid empty result (the site's 'There were no records found' message with 'Search Results - 0 Records'), not an error. `data_as_of` is the site's nightly refresh stamp.

respondent_narratives.name: INTERACTIVE BROKERS CORP
respondent_narratives.text:
Release Number 8794-23
CFTC Orders Interactive Brokers to Pay $20 Million for Recordkeeping and Supervision Failures for Widespread Use of Unapproved Communication Methods
September 29, 2023

Washington, D.C. — The Commodity Futures Trading Commission today issued an order simultaneously filing and settling charges against Interactive Brokers Corp., an introducing broker, and Interactive Brokers LLC, a futures commission merchant, for failing to maintain and preserve records that were required to be kept under CFTC recordkeeping requirements, and failing to diligently supervise matters related to their businesses as CFTC registrants.

The order requires Interactive Brokers to pay a $20 million civil monetary penalty, to cease and desist from further violations of recordkeeping and supervision requirements, and to engage in specified remedial undertakings. Interactive Brokers admits the facts detailed in the order.

Case Background

The order finds from at least 2019 to the present, Interactive Brokers failed to stop its employees, including those at senior levels, from communicating using unapproved communication methods, including messages sent via personal text and WhatsApp. The firm was required to keep certain of these written communications because they related to the firm’s CFTC-registered businesses. These written communications generally were not maintained and preserved by Interactive Brokers, and the firm generally would not have been able to provide them promptly to the CFTC if and when requested. 

The order also finds the widespread use of unapproved communication methods violated Interactive Brokers’ internal policies and procedures, which generally prohibited business-related communication taking place via unapproved methods. Further, some of the same supervisory personnel responsible for ensuring compliance with the firm’s policies and procedures themselves used non-approved methods of communication to engage in business-related communications, in violation of firm policy.

Since December 2021, the CFTC has imposed $1.117 billion in civil monetary penalties on 20 financial institutions for their use of unapproved methods of communication, in violation of CFTC recordkeeping and supervision requirements. [See CFTC Press Release Nos. 8470-21; 8599-22; 8699-23; 8701-23; 8762-23; 8763-23]

Related Civil Actions

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) today also announced entry of an order filing and settling charges against Interactive Brokers and imposing a civil monetary penalty for recordkeeping and supervision violations related to the use of unapproved methods of communication.

******

The CFTC Division of Enforcement staff responsible for this action are Devin Cain; Alejandra de Urioste; R. Stephen Painter, Jr.; Lenel Hickson, Jr.; and Manal M. Sultan.

-CFTC-

post.description: Search the CMS NPPES NPI Registry for healthcare providers (individuals or organizations) by name, organization, taxonomy/specialty, city, state, postal code or country. Returns one page (limit 1–200, skip up to 1200) of full provider records: NPI, taxonomies with licenses, mailing and practice addresses, other names, payer identifiers and endpoints. Requires at least one of first_name, last_name, organization_name, taxonomy_description or postal_code.

address_purpose.description:
Which address the city/state/postal_code filters apply to. Default: any.

Provider reference: allowed values ["location", "mailing", "primary", "secondary"].

city.description: City of the mailing or practice address. Up to 100 ASCII characters (NPPES rejects accented letters; O'Brien, Smith-Jones and St. John are fine); one trailing `*` wildcard is allowed after at least two characters.

country_code.description: Two-letter country code; US is the default in NPPES. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

enumeration_type.description:
individual (NPI-1) or organization (NPI-2). Omit for both.

Provider reference: allowed values ["individual", "organization"].

first_name.description: Individual provider first name (NPI-1 only). Up to 100 ASCII characters (NPPES rejects accented letters; O'Brien, Smith-Jones and St. John are fine); one trailing `*` wildcard is allowed after at least two characters.

last_name.description: Individual provider last name (NPI-1 only). Up to 100 ASCII characters (NPPES rejects accented letters; O'Brien, Smith-Jones and St. John are fine); one trailing `*` wildcard is allowed after at least two characters.

limit.description:
Records per page.

Provider reference: minimum 1; maximum 200; default 10.

organization_name.description: Organization legal name or other name (NPI-2 only); also matches Doing Business As names. Up to 100 ASCII characters (NPPES rejects accented letters; O'Brien, Smith-Jones and St. John are fine); one trailing `*` wildcard is allowed after at least two characters.

postal_code.description: 5- or 9-digit ZIP, or a prefix followed by `*` (e.g. 941*).

skip.description:
Records to skip; pass next_skip from the previous page. NPPES allows at most 1200.

Provider reference: minimum 0; maximum 1200; default 0.

state.description: Two-letter US state/territory code. Needs another criterion. Pattern: ^[A-Za-z]{2}$.

taxonomy_description.description: Specialty / taxonomy description such as Cardiology, Dermatology, Family Medicine, Hospice Care, Community Based, or a taxonomy code like 208800000X. Up to 100 ASCII characters (NPPES rejects accented letters; O'Brien, Smith-Jones and St. John are fine); one trailing `*` wildcard is allowed after at least two characters.

use_first_name_alias.description: Also match common first-name aliases (Bob for Robert). Requires first_name. NPPES default is true.

value.description:
Slack Business - Enterprise facilitates team communication and collaboration with integration capabilities and a user-friendly interface, supporting mobile and web platforms. It enhances productivity through efficient organization, instant communication, and extensive customization options.Designed for seamless integration with apps and services, Slack Business - Enterprise provides efficient organization through channels and threads, instant communication, file sharing, and video calls. Productivity is boosted via notifications, reminders, bots, and automation. Customization enhances the user experience, promoting collaboration. However, improvement areas include video chat, meeting functions, and third-party tool integration. Users prioritize enhanced UI, security, and document collaboration, alongside better scalability, stability, and attachment browsing capabilities.What are the key features of Slack Business - Enterprise?
Seamless Integration: Connect with a range of apps and services to streamline operations.
Efficient Organization: Utilize channels and threads for organized communication.
Instant Communication: Facilitate real-time messaging for immediate interaction.
File Sharing: Share documents and media effortlessly within the platform.
Video Calls: Support for video meetings with screen sharing capabilities.
Automation: Boost productivity with notifications, reminders, and bots.
Customization: Tailor UI and integrations to enhance the user experience.
Search Function: Easily locate past messages and information.
What benefits and ROI should users consider?
Enhanced Collaboration: Facilitates teamwork with organized channels and real-time messaging.
Improved Productivity: Automation and integrations streamline workflow processes.
Flexibility: Mobile and web platform support suits diverse work environments.
Customizability: Tailor functionalities to specific needs for better engagement.
Integration Capabilities: Connect with tools like Google Drive and Zoom to enhance workflows.
Slack Business - Enterprise is widely used across various industries, serving as a communication hub within organizations. Its features support internal and external communication, project management, and workflow optimization. Industries benefit from its integration with Google Drive and Zoom, enabling efficient collaboration and streamlined operations.
